finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL. Its only host check is a suffix match with no dot boundary (endswith("example.com")), so hostnames such as evilexample.com or evil-example.com pass, and the attacker can point such a domain's DNS at internal addresses (127.0.0.1, RFC1918, 169.254.169.254).
finding.source: mirror.py:11 — url query parameter of GET /mirror (no authentication)
finding.sink: mirror.py:16 — await c.get(url) via httpx.AsyncClient, using the raw unparsed url string

trace.note: url enters from the query string
host = urlparse(url).hostname or "" extracts the hostname
Only gate: host.endswith("example.com") — plain suffix match, no leading dot; raises 400 on failure
httpx.AsyncClient() created with default settings (no redirect following, no IP filtering)
Outbound GET to the original url string, not the validated parsed value
Returns len(r.text), leaking response length as an oracle

finding.guards_checked: Hostname suffix check at line 13: present but insufficient (no dot boundary). No scheme allow-list. No resolved-IP/private-range/link-local check (name-only). Redirects: httpx default follow_redirects=False, so the case-04 redirect-escape path does not apply (confirm against deployed httpx version). Parser differential between urllib.parse and httpx: no concrete exploiting payload found, not reported. No auth on endpoint.

verdict.guard_found: Only guard is mirror.py:13, `host.endswith("example.com")`, a bare suffix match with no dot boundary, which does not close the finding. The constant ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 (".example.com") is defined but never used, so it is not a guard. No scheme restriction, exact-host set, or resolved-IP/private-range check exists anywhere in the path.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter at mirror.py:11 is unauthenticated, and the only host check at mirror.py:13 is a suffix match, so an attacker can use a domain like evilexample.com whose DNS resolves to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254; mirror.py:16 then sends the raw url via c.get(url) and mirror.py:17 returns len(r.text) as a response-size oracle. Every trace line matches the code as described.
